races.name: Morgan's Army Fighting Spirit Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rhodes Runner
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner with four of five career runs on good ground and consistent form figures (4-3-2-4 recently), Rossa Ryan takes the ride for Ralph Beckett who is in decent 14-day form; 19-day turnaround is sharp enough and this horse has the natural role in the race but must settle the pace argument with Downonmainstreet quickly or both risk stopping.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's juvenile won on good ground first time out but has posted finishing positions of 12, 21, and 15 since, and is specifically tagged as fading in the finish — the blinkers are off, the hold-up style leaves too much to do on this flat six-furlong track, and the form trajectory is sharply negative.

runners_data.name: Downonmainstreet
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly won last time out over five furlongs on good ground and has been placed in two of three starts; David Egan takes over and the horse maps to lead, but stepping up to six furlongs for the first time while simultaneously fighting Rhodes Runner for the early lead introduces real stamina and tactical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: George Scott's colt has been placed in four of five starts including back-to-back seconds at six furlongs on good, wears a hood, and the 41-day freshener may suit a horse who tends to travel prominently and finish honestly; Liam Wright claims 3lb off an OR of 73 which helps in a tight nursery.

runners_data.name: Laylaty
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's filly won at six furlongs on good ground last time out and has two further placed efforts in three career starts, making her the most recently successful horse in the field; Lewis Edmunds rides and the prominent style sits perfectly in the tactical shape this race creates behind the front-runner duel.

runners_data.name: Minzaal Time
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes sends out this hold-up type whose recent form on standard and good ground reads 5-7-8-12 — finishing in the rear in every outing and without a single career place; wearing a hood and down in the weights at OR 68, but there is no empirical evidence this horse can reach competitive horses from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Seed Ya Later
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark's mount for Jack Channon has placed in four of six career runs and won once, but the form string includes a recent seventh on good ground; a ten-day turnaround is the sharpest in the field and the prominent style suits the race shape, though the horse's inconsistency — bouncing between 1st and 7th — makes reliance difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Rhodes Runner and Downonmainstreet are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the jump, creating a genuinely competitive early pace over six furlongs on good ground at Ffos Las. Neither is likely to yield willingly, so the gallop should be honest rather than suicidal — enough to stretch the field but not necessarily blow up the pace-setters entirely. Prominent runners Tango Hotel, Laylaty, and Seed Ya Later will track closely just off the duel, meaning the race will be strung out early with hold-up horses Wild Terrain and Minzaal Time operating from the rear. The honest contested pace with a compressed mid-pack suits horses who can race prominently in the slipstream of the duel and finish strongly — a profile that advantages the P-style horses poised just behind the leaders rather than deep closers, who will have too much ground to make up on a flat six-furlong track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-runners Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Rhodes Runner or Downonmainstreet controls the duel and sustains enough pace to hold off the chasers, the winner comes from the lead or direct slipstream.
scenarios.body: The contested front ensures the pace is genuine, and the flat Ffos Las six furlongs does not blunt pace-setters the way a track with a stiff finish would; whichever of the two leads more economically from an early position is best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poachers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner duel burns both leaders out in the final furlong, a prominent racer tracking just behind delivers the winning move.
scenarios.body: Tango Hotel and Laylaty are both P-style horses with recent winning form on good ground and sit ideally positioned to pounce when the leaders tie up; Tango Hotel's back-to-back placed efforts at six furlongs on good and Laylaty's course-distance win give both live credentials here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel burns unusually fierce and the field strings out significantly, a closer with late energy picks off the tiring leaders in the final hundred yards.
scenarios.body: Wild Terrain won on good ground and has the profile, but has since finished 12th, 21st, and 15th — her fading-in-finish tag and recent dire form make this scenario dependent on a dramatic collapse at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Rhodes Runner and Downonmainstreet both drop out tamely after a short sharp burst and no horse takes control, the race devolves into a sprint from halfway.
scenarios.body: Seed Ya Later, with multiple placed efforts on good ground and a recent ten-day turnaround suggesting fitness, could benefit from a messy pace in a scenario where form lines are scrambled; this is the least structured outcome and the least probable given both front-runners have recent strong pace-setting evidence.

watchPoints.text: Rhodes Runner and Downonmainstreet — watch how aggressively each jockey contests the lead in the first furlong; if Egan pushes Downonmainstreet hard to dominate, both front-runners risk a mutually destructive early pace that opens the door for the prominent chasers.

Laylaty — a six-furlong winner on good ground last time and ideally placed to track the duel, but if she is caught wide early due to draw or traffic, she loses the prominent berth that is central to her winning chance.

Wild Terrain's fading-in-finish flag is significant — even if the pace collapses in front, this hold-up horse has shown a pattern of dropping away late rather than staying on, making a late swoop highly speculative.

Tango Hotel's 41-day absence is the longest in the field — watch for signs in the early market moves whether George Scott has this horse spot-on; a hood-wearing prominent type who is race-fit could be seriously underestimated in a compressed nursery market.

Minzaal Time's entire form profile is on artificial or softer surfaces at seven furlongs — the switch to six furlongs on good turf represents a significant profile mismatch and Finley Marsh will face a tactical challenge generating any meaningful late run.

races.name: Shirgar Welsh Butter Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Channel Islands
runners_data.note: Made his debut at 7f on good ground, finishing fifth, so dropping to 6f on a flat, right-handed track suits better; David Evans handler is solid at this level and Darragh Keenan gets the ride, but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence given the horse is racing slightly out of its most comfortable lead role against light opposition.

runners_data.name: Corbie Rock
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with an unknown going profile and no form string available; Jane Chapple-Hyam sends runners to Ffos Las with purpose and Rhys Clutterbuck keeps the booking, so this debut could spring a surprise if the yard has done its homework, but the complete absence of evidence makes this a pure unknown.

runners_data.name: Native Chief
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over for John Butler on a horse whose sole run came over 7f at Southwell, finishing eighth; the fades-in-finish flag is a structural concern on a track that tends to reward those who travel well into the straight, and stepping down to 6f may not be the obvious cure.

runners_data.name: Tumishi
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's two-year-old has twice finished in the placings over 6f on good ground, showing genuine course-distance form, but carries the redistribution caveat — a natural prominent type who may find War Gaming and Channel Islands ahead of him positionally; Daniel Muscutt will need to adapt tactics if the expected early slots are filled before he can press forward.

runners_data.name: War Gaming
runners_data.note: Three runs all on good ground over 5-6f, accumulating three places from three starts — consistent without winning — and Rossa Ryan's booking on a horse with genuine course-distance fitness makes this one of the most straightforward pace fits in the field; the high-pace flag aligns with a prominent position just off Channel Islands.

runners_data.name: Duchess Of Immatin
runners_data.note: George Boughey's operation is among the sharpest for placing well-bred debutants, and Kieran Shoemark's retained-jockey booking adds authority to this entry; the unknown going profile is simply a function of inexperience rather than any red flag, and 128lbs versus 133lbs for the field gives a marginal weight advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Channel Islands is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead, should be able to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo over the straight Ffos Las six furlongs on good ground. War Gaming and Tumishi both carry prominent profiles but Tumishi has been redistributed to midfield on the map — the field holds more pace-hungry types than the shape can accommodate, and War Gaming is the one most likely to slot in just behind Channel Islands in the prime stalking position. That uncontested, sustainable gallop created by Channel Islands sets up a race where a horse able to travel close to the pace without expending energy in a battle for position holds a clear structural advantage, meaning a prominent or close-stalking profile benefits most; deep hold-up tactics are structurally disadvantaged unless the pace collapses entirely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Rail Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Channel Islands dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the rail position proves the advantage it typically is at Ffos Las over 6f.
scenarios.body: Channel Islands bowls along without pressure, conserving enough to fight back inside the final furlong, while War Gaming tracks in the ideal stalking slot and finishes with purpose.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Channel Islands sets too fast an early gallop on the testing good ground and fades sharply inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A late rush develops through the final furlong as the leader tires, benefiting any horse that has conserved energy from off the pace; Duchess Of Immatin or Corbie Rock, both lightly raced debutants with unknown profiles, could emerge from the pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two unexposed newcomers, Corbie Rock or Duchess Of Immatin, brings a level of natural ability that overrides tactical positioning.
scenarios.body: George Boughey's Duchess Of Immatin, drawn in a field with limited opposition depth, could produce a debut performance that simply outclasses the runners around her; Corbie Rock under Jane Chapple-Hyam represents a similar wildcard from a trainer who can place debutants well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and create a true finishing runway for a horse coming from the back.
scenarios.body: Native Chief, flagged as one who fades in the finish and with only a recent Southwell run to point to, is not ideally placed to benefit; this scenario carries low probability because the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to manufacture a true test for closers and no reliable hold-up performer is in the field.

watchPoints.text: Channel Islands and War Gaming may clash for the same prominent ground in the early strides — watch whether War Gaming is able to press into the stalking position or is forced wider and later into the race.

Tumishi's redistribution means Daniel Muscutt could find himself three or four lengths further back than his natural style demands; if he is unable to press up from midfield turning into the straight, his form figures over course and distance become less meaningful.

Native Chief's fades-in-finish flag combined with a sole run at Southwell over 7f makes his ability to see out the 6f on good ground at Ffos Las genuinely uncertain — watch for signs of stopping inside the final furlong rather than finishing through.

Both Duchess Of Immatin and Corbie Rock are debut runners with UNKNOWN going and style profiles — if either breaks with natural speed and slots into a prominent position, the race shape could shift materially away from what the map projects.

races.name: Cjch Solicitors Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up specialist on going it handles well, but with so many closers in this field it will struggle to find clear air late; blinkers on, 22 days fresh, and Scott Dixon's yard is firing at 1/21 over 14 days — the tactical squeeze is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Diamondsinthesand
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who wants to come from off the pace, but its recent form string of 777686 offers little encouragement and five efforts on similar ground (1W2P from 15) are uninspiring; Adrian Wintle's stable is 0/8 in the past fortnight, and the horse's natural closing style is crowded out by the volume of rear-runners in this field.

runners_data.name: Macarone
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's five-year-old has a placed effort on Good last time and its stable is showing reasonable 14-day form at 3/15; it races from the back but is one of the hold-up types whose preferred position is uncompromised by redistribution, meaning it retains better scope to finish than several rivals if the pace is strong enough.

runners_data.name: Outer Edge
runners_data.note: Consistent each-way profile with a string of placed efforts on Good ground (1W2P from 6 on similar), and Gina Mangan claims the ride; the horse races from behind and its 42-day break is a flag — whether it has retained peak condition after over six weeks off is the key question.

runners_data.name: Sundiata Keita
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in this race, wearing a hood and only 10 days since its last start; its STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges it is being asked to lead rather than race prominently, but in practice it secures the role by default and dictates the complexion of the race entirely.

runners_data.name: Demetris Mouflon
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's three-year-old is 80 days without a run — the longest absence in the field — and its best form has come at 7-8f rather than 6f; a genuine hold-up type whose natural position is congested by rivals of the same profile, and the combination of the step down in trip and the layoff makes it hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride for Dylan Cunha, who is in fair 14-day form at 5/21; the three-year-old has a placed effort on Good over 5f and races from hold-up, but its most recent run (6th on Good over 6f) is directly relevant, and it is one of the few horses in the field whose current profile and jockey booking lift it above the pack.

runners_data.name: Ridger
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and its form figures of 6997 are modest — all four career runs are in the book, none producing a placed finish; the three-year-old's best going form is on Good (1/4) but that single run is a slender sample, and Stevie Donohoe inherits a horse that has been racing at 6-7f on artificials without distinction.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Daniel Muscutt picks up the ride for R Harris, a yard with no 14-day runners logged; the three-year-old shows solid consistency with multiple placed efforts on Good (0W2P from 8 on that surface) and over 6f, and though its natural style is hold-up — placing it among the congested rear of field — its course-relevant form and Muscutt's ability to find a run make it one of the more interesting horses if the pace suits.

races.paceDynamic: Sundiata Keita is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f Ffos Las contest and should stride to the lead unchallenged from the gates, setting a sustainable gallop on Good turf without any rival likely to press or harry for early supremacy. The pace note flags that this field carries far more hold-up bias than the map can accommodate — Demetris Mouflon, Rogue Rebellion, Ridger, Coast, and Diamondsinthesand are all genuine come-from-behind types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all operate from their natural rear position. With Sundiata Keita able to dictate a measured tempo and the bulk of the field compelled to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, the race shape is one of controlled fractions into the straight, limiting the depth of closing run available to the true hold-up horses. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent or pace-tracking profile — horses that can sit just behind the leader, travel within themselves, and pick up early in the straight will be best placed, while genuine closers face a compromised setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sundiata Keita Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sundiata Keita leads without pressure and the pace stays honest but not extreme, allowing it to dominate from the front.
scenarios.body: Sundiata Keita bowls along in front at a sustainable clip, and no rival has the early pace to challenge; horses tracking it into the straight get first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sits prominently or just off the leader and pounces when Sundiata Keita ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The steady pace means the leader gives a good account but is caught late by a horse that has tracked throughout and has a gear change to offer; the hold-up horses arrive too late having been forced wider or further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to string the field out and one of the genuine closers threads through for a late surge.
scenarios.body: Despite the overcrowded rear of field, one of the redistributed hold-up types — most likely Rogue Rebellion or Macarone — finds a clear run and finishes strongly, but this shape needs a tempo the lone front-runner is unlikely to generate alone.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse and Melee
scenarios.trigger: If Sundiata Keita fades badly and the field bunches in a sprint finish that becomes a lottery.
scenarios.body: A false pace produces a blanket finish in the final furlong with no horse gaining a decisive advantage early; any horse with residual toe and a clear run benefits, making form hard to read.

watchPoints.text: Sundiata Keita is the only horse with a credible claim to lead from the front — watch whether it jumps cleanly and establishes position immediately, because if it misses the break the entire race shape dissolves and a chaotic sprint finish becomes likely.

The five redistributed hold-up types (Coast, Diamondsinthesand, Demetris Mouflon, Ridger, Rogue Rebellion) will all be seeking to race from the rear — watch for traffic chaos and interference entering the straight as these horses converge on limited room.

Outer Edge's 42-day absence is the longest layoff among the field's hold-up horses; watch for signs of rustiness in the early stages, as a horse needing the run will be further disadvantaged by the compromised closing position.

Demetris Mouflon is stepping back to 6f from 7-8f after an 80-day break — watch whether it travels fluently early, as a horse out of its best trip and returning from a significant absence may struggle to sustain its run.

David Egan on Mayflower Rock is the most notable jockey booking among the hold-up brigade — watch whether he positions the horse closer than its style tag implies, as Egan is likely to adapt to the race shape rather than be trapped in a congested closing group.

races.name: Roly Poly Events Race Of Hope Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Good Onya Mate
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer whose recent form includes a solid 2nd over 14f on Good; Kieran Shoemark is a significant jockey booking for this grade, hood reportedly worn, but a tendency to finish mid-pack rather than win limits confidence even in a shape that suits.|

runners_data.name: Golden Flame
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a genuine win and five places from 15 runs on similar Going, and a course-appropriate 16f win in recent form — Zoe Lewis (7lb claim) brings the weight right down, and this hold-up type's best chance comes if the pace sets up for a sustained late run.|

runners_data.name: Lusaka
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse who has placed at 14f and 16f on Good going multiple times and carries the hood; John & Flint trainer combo in form (1/9 over 14 days) and the 49-day freshener could suit a stayer of this profile if the closing run is there.|

runners_data.name: Merrijig
runners_data.note: Strong recent form at 16-18f on Good (3 places from 9 runs on similar ground) and a genuine 16f Stall winner; though the map places him in midfield, Berry's veteran is a true hold-up horse by nature — his best chance depends on getting closer to the pace than his natural style would suggest, which the compressed field may allow.|

runners_data.name: Sneaky Blinder
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, fresh from just 9 days ago, with Rossa Ryan booked to control tempo over 2m on Good; his sim-going record is thin (2 runs, 1 place) but unchallenged leads on this track can be very hard to peg back, and his low weight (134lbs) aids his staying effort.|

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old whose form is entirely on Soft/Standard, making this Good ground a potential concern; Harry Vigors (5lb claim) helps, the hood is worn, but as a hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position, he's racing in a role that doesn't come naturally and his shorter-trip background (12-16f mostly on yielding) is a query at 2m Good.|

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has placed three horses in the last 30 days and this 6-year-old has strong form credentials at 16-18f on Good (8 runs, 1 win, 4 places); a true hold-up horse whose natural position is further back than the map shows, the tongue-tie and visor combination signals trainer intent, and Kavanagh's 3lb claim brings him in at a competitive weight.|

runners_data.name: Last Flight
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3-year-old whose entire form is on Standard or Good, but all five runs have been at 10-16f — stepping up to 2m on a turning track is a significant stamina test; Stevie Donohoe has course experience and the 120lb weight is attractive, but no headgear and no hold-up wins at this trip make this a risky proposition.|

runners_data.name: Make A Splash
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — a serious concern in a 2m staying handicap; Tom Ward in decent 14-day form (2/14) and the lowest weight in the race (114lbs) offers theoretical upside, but a 3-year-old with a form string of 9688 and a noted finishing weakness is difficult to trust here, and displacement to midfield on the map compounds the difficulty.|

races.paceDynamic: Sneaky Blinder is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m handicap at Ffos Las and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, will settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the outset on Good ground. The remaining eight runners are all hold-up types by nature, meaning a long, steady gallop is set with one horse controlling the tempo throughout — a classically vulnerable lead scenario only if the pace is truly dawdling, but on 2m at Ffos Las a solo front-runner can dictate and conserve energy effectively. This race shape strongly favours genuine, proven hold-up horses with the stamina to close over the final three to four furlongs once Sneaky Blinder's lead is eventually challenged turning for home. Note that the field holds far more true hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Merrijig, Beaune, Simiyann, Last Flight and Make A Splash are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and in reality Merrijig and Simiyann, with the most consistent form at this trip and going, are best placed to secure the closest midfield tracking positions that will prove most tactically advantageous.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sneaky Blinder Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sneaky Blinder dictates a sustainable solo gallop and the hold-up pack fails to mount a coordinated challenge until too late.
scenarios.body: Sneaky Blinder, uncontested up front on Good ground over 2m, conserves energy through an honest but manageable pace before pulling clear when rivals are still organising their challenges in the straight; prominent horses who have tracked within striking distance benefit most as hold-up horses from deep find the straight too short to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slow enough to compress the field and genuine hold-up horses with strong 2m+ form produce late runs to overhaul Sneaky Blinder.
scenarios.body: The compacted field turns for home in a bunch, and horses with proven stamina and strong finishing tendencies — particularly those with consistent placings at 16-18f on Good — use the final two furlongs to run past a tiring front-runner; runners with the best sim-going records on this surface have the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tracking Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If two or three horses post up just behind Sneaky Blinder in the first mile and kick decisively turning into the straight, leaving the deep hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Horses positioned in the first four at halfway can time their challenge to perfection around the turning track at Ffos Las, hitting the front before the true closers have begun their runs; this suits any runner that has contested prominent positions in recent form and has course familiarity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If Sneaky Blinder goes too hard early and capitulates in the straight, creating a messy finish where a lightly-weighted younger horse sneaks through.
scenarios.body: A field of hold-up types suddenly finding a riderless pace-setting vacuum can create positional chaos, and a low-weighted 3-year-old with fresh legs could benefit from the confusion; however this is the least likely shape given Sneaky Blinder's jockey and team are expected to ride conservatively.

watchPoints.text: Sneaky Blinder sets the entire race shape — watch whether Rossa Ryan elects to bowl along or nurse the pace, as this single decision will determine whether the hold-up horses have any chance of closing.|

Golden Flame and Lusaka both have strong form at 16f on Good but are ridden by apprentices (Lewis 7lb, Fisher) — watch whether either can overcome positional inexperience in a race where timing the challenge from the rear is critical.|

Merrijig and Simiyann are natural hold-up horses who will need to take up a closer position than usual given the field composition — watch the first half-mile to see whether either can slot into a tracking role behind Sneaky Blinder without burning extra energy.|

Make A Splash's noted tendency to fade in the finish is a live concern at 2m — watch this runner in the final three furlongs as any fading could impede hold-up horses making their runs on the inside.|

Last Flight steps up sharply in trip to 2m for the first time — watch whether the 3-year-old is able to handle the stamina test and the turning nature of Ffos Las, as a stopping performance could cause interference to closers.|

races.name: Bni Elli Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose recent form (2nd twice over 12f on good) shows competence at this level, but the redistribution to midfield places it closer to the pace than ideal — its OR 86 also represents a significant class ceiling against the 120-rated rivals here.

runners_data.name: Pacific Storm
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's lightly raced three-year-old steps back up to 1m4f where it finished 7th last time, and David Egan's booking adds interest, though 69 days off and a sole placing-free form string offer limited confidence at this class level.

runners_data.name: Phantom Recon
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for George Scott, whose T14 return of 2/26 reflects recent activity; racing from OR 120 with two fourth-place finishes over course-relevant trips, this horse will dictate the tempo and its chance hinges entirely on whether that lead is sustainable to the line.

runners_data.name: Winday
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins' runner has its best form over 2m+ on heavy or soft ground and arrives 89 days fresh; the step down to 1m4f on good turf looks a significant ask for a horse whose experience is almost entirely on Flat-cap Irish tracks in heavy conditions.

runners_data.name: Neswick
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's lightly raced colt brings a 3-4 form string from standard-going tracks and runs off 128lbs having been seen just 14 days ago — the recency is a positive, and Daniel Muscutt's booking for a lightly exposed type with class ratings to match the top-raters makes this one of the more interesting profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Saaffya
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's debutant carries a completely unknown going profile and no public form, but Kieran Shoemark riding for a trainer with a 2/41 14-day strike rate on a track that suits patient placement means this runner cannot be ignored despite the absence of any handicapper's evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Phantom Recon is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and looks set to stride into a comfortable lead from the outset over 1m4f on good ground at Ffos Las, with nothing else willing to press them for supremacy. With Phantom Recon dictating a sustainable, uncontested tempo, the race will likely unfold in a processional fashion through the middle stages before the hold-up brigade — Pacific Storm, Winday, and Blue Hercules — attempt to close from behind. However, the field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear: Blue Hercules, a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield in the map, is unlikely to get all the way to the back, meaning the true deep closers are fewer than they appear. This race shape most favours a prominent or pace-pressing profile — a horse that can sit just off Phantom Recon's shoulder, avoid the pace-vacuum from too far back, and deploy a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Phantom Recon Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Recon secures an uncontested lead and sets a measured, even tempo that grinds down the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Phantom Recon settles into a comfortable rhythm with no rival willing to challenge early, meaning the fractions are controlled entirely by George Scott's runner and any closer must produce an exceptional finish to reel them in. Horses positioned prominently or just off the pace — and any unexposed types with class to match — are best placed to capitalise if Phantom Recon does tire in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Recon sets a stronger-than-expected pace and the higher-rated hold-up horses (Pacific Storm, Neswick) find enough room to deliver a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A fractionally brisker tempo would compress the field into a bunched finish entering the straight, allowing a classy horse tracking from midfield to pick them off in the closing stages. Pacific Storm, OR 120 and lightly raced over this trip, and Saaffya — a debut runner from Ed Walker with an unknown going profile — represent the types most suited to this shape if ground conditions produce a testing finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unexposed Debutant Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Saaffya debuts with significant unseen ability and Kieran Shoemark produces a well-timed run from an unknown base.
scenarios.body: Ed Walker's debutant carries an unknown going profile and no form to assess, but the stable's strike rate and Shoemark's placement suggest the horse may arrive ahead of market expectations. A straightforward, even-paced race over 1m4f on good ground would be the most benign possible introduction for an unknown quantity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fail to Close
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Recon's pace proves genuinely sustainable and the true hold-up horses — Pacific Storm, Winday, Blue Hercules — leave themselves with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Blue Hercules, displaced from its natural rear position into midfield, and Winday, whose best form has come over much longer trips on heavy ground, may both struggle to land a telling blow if the pace never truly falls apart. In this scenario the race becomes a procession and the winner comes from the front two or three throughout, leaving the deeper hold-up horses empty-handed despite late effort.

watchPoints.text: Watch Phantom Recon's early splits — if Darragh Keenan allows them to bowl along unchallenged, the gap to the hold-up horses could become unmanageable before the home straight.
Blue Hercules is mapped to midfield but is a genuine hold-up horse; if it settles further back than shown, its OR 86 makes it a unlikely winner against 120-rated rivals even with a clean run.

Winday's going record is almost entirely on heavy ground and its two efforts on going-to-good (one 3rd over 9f) offer thin evidence that it can handle this surface — monitor paddock condition and early movement closely.
Saaffya debuts with no public form — Kieran Shoemark's positioning in the first two furlongs will be the earliest signal of whether the horse is forward enough to figure in the finish.

Pacific Storm's 69-day absence combined with a form string of just two runs means fitness cannot be assumed; watch whether David Egan settles quietly or begins to ask questions early, which would indicate the horse is ready to run its race.

races.name: Ex1 Digital Forensic Services Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fast Steps
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with six placed efforts at 10-12f on Good going in recent form, though winless; Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim is a useful weight-saving angle and the step back up to 1m2f after shorter trips suits his staying profile.

runners_data.name: Symphony's Song
runners_data.note: Holds prominent style naturally and has placed twice on Good ground at 10f, but the two runs on Standard (AW) suggest connections have been searching for form; stepping up from 8f, the extra distance here looks a positive for a horse by a middle-distance sire.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — leads from the front and has been placed in seven of twelve Good-ground starts with a win at 9f; Donagh Murphy's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable and with no rival to press the pace, controlled fractions are virtually guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: Veteran of ten at this level, naturally a hold-up operator whose best form comes when covered up and produced late, but the crowded hold-up quarter means he is unlikely to find his ideal spot; six placed efforts in fifteen Good-ground runs speak to consistency rather than winning potential here.

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose form figures of 45-646 show no wins and no places on Good ground, and the step up to 1m2f is unproven; the 'b' headgear flag suggests the yard is seeking a concentration boost, but the evidence base is thin for confidence in this shape.

runners_data.name: Sahm Naif
runners_data.note: Two wins from six runs on Good ground at 10f make this three-year-old's profile look tailor-made for today's conditions; prominent in running by style, the 7lb apprentice Alfie Redman brings a weight advantage, though positional discipline will be key tracking Takeitorleaveit.

runners_data.name: Grand Pier
runners_data.note: Second over 10f on Soft on comeback, missed 71 days since, and Harry Vigors (3lb claim) takes the ride; has no wins in seven career starts and the wide-draw potential at Ffos Las could cost lengths early if he drifts off a true line.

runners_data.name: Tales Old As Time
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by inclination whose last four runs have produced a third at 7f and three single-figure finishes at shorter trips; stepping up markedly in trip to 1m2f on only the fourth career start, stamina is genuinely unproven and the style compromise adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Has run four times on Good ground in recent form and placed once at 10f, showing enough to be considered; Charlie Bell's 7lb claim helps, but the horse is a hold-up type in a race where closers face a structural disadvantage and the record of 0W1P in seven Good-ground outings flags limited upside.

runners_data.name: Hotel California
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with only three career starts and one placing at 10f on Good, trained by David Menuisier who excels with improvers; a natural hold-up operator mapped to midfield due to competition for rear berths, and on bare form the current evidence base is too thin to rate this highly.

races.paceDynamic: Takeitorleaveit is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no rival pressing for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, measured gallop on Good ground at Ffos Las — a flat track that rewards those who can maintain rhythm without being harassed. Fast Steps, Symphony's Song, and Sahm Naif will push forward to prominent positions just off the leader, creating a compact early order with a genuine pace hierarchy rather than a chaotic scramble. The large hold-up contingent — Grand Pier, Brave Leader, The Anthony Gover, and those redistributed to midfield — will be forced to cover ground from further back, and on a track where sustained finishing kicks are tested rather than sudden bursts, the gap to the front could prove significant. The race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track the leader at a comfortable clip and pounce entering the straight, with true hold-up horses carrying a structural disadvantage unless the pace collapses. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely race at the rear in a tidy fashion; Tales Old As Time, Hotel California, and Revich are the redistributed runners, and of those, Revich's course form gives it the best chance of finding a workable position despite its natural style being compromised.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Takeitorleaveit Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit leads unchallenged and sets a sustainable pace that drains the closers' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Donagh Murphy (claiming 5lb) can dictate every fraction on a flat track with no pressure, and the modest gallop will suit horses tracking within two lengths of the leader entering the home straight. Prominent types who travel kindly just off the pace — particularly those with Good-ground form — are best placed to capitalise as the lead horse either holds on or is picked off close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just steady enough for the front two or three to stay in contention while the true leader fades late.
scenarios.body: Sahm Naif and Fast Steps, both proven at this trip on Good going and carrying reasonable weights, can stalk the leader and wear down Takeitorleaveit inside the final furlong. This shape rewards horses with a combination of prominent positioning and demonstrated stamina at 1m2f, and Sahm Naif's two wins at 10f on Good underline that profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to open a gap in the pack and a well-positioned midfield runner finds a clear passage.
scenarios.body: Grand Pier, with a recent second over 10f on Soft, could improve on a sounder surface and thread through a tiring field if fractions quicken mid-race. The Anthony Gover has plentiful Good-ground form at this level but has shown a tendency to find only one or two, and this shape would need everything to fall perfectly for a horse coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse or Incident
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit is slow away, checked, or the field bunches and a sprint develops turning for home.
scenarios.body: A compressed field at the top of the straight would negate the front-runner's advantage and open the race up to any horse with a sharp turn of foot, including redistributed runners like Hotel California and Tales Old As Time who prefer this compressed, late-running scenario. However, neither has strong evidence of delivering on this surface or distance, making this a low-probability but non-trivial disruption scenario.

watchPoints.text: Takeitorleaveit — if Donagh Murphy is slow to assert from the gates and a prominent rival like Fast Steps or Sahm Naif steals the rail, the entire pace dynamic shifts and the tactical plan unravels immediately.

Sahm Naif — Alfie Redman (7lb claim, conditional) will need to judge the pace perfectly tracking a controlled leader; any positional error or wide passage could negate the Going and trip advantage this horse holds on paper.

Grand Pier — 71 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field and, while the comeback second was encouraging, fitness at a flat track that can expose stamina concerns should be monitored in the early stages.

Tales Old As Time, Hotel California, Revich — all three are genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield by the shape of this race; watch whether any can find an off-the-rail passage approaching the turn, as a tightly bunched midfield makes clean passage the decisive variable for this group.

Brave Leader — headgear (blinkers) fitted for the first time or reapplied; watch market moves and early behaviour in the stalls, as blinkers on a lightly exposed three-year-old can produce either a marked step forward or an overcooking of the early pace.
